answer: A sybil-proof agent economy makes fake identities expensive to run and cheap to catch. Every agent must stake value before earning, so each extra puppet is a fresh dune of locked capital an attacker cannot reuse. Work is checked by random peer audits: a plume of independent verifiers samples answers, and copied or lazy work forfeits the stake, so farming a thousand fakes costs a thousand stakes. Honest history compounds into reputation that a new raven identity cannot buy, so the marginal cost of the next fake always exceeds what it can earn.
